title: Chart Reader Candle & Pattern Behaviour Research Registry
purpose: Original concise research descriptions and testable hypotheses. Not copied book text and not measured performance claims.
interpretation_policy: Pattern labels describe geometry and conventional context hypotheses. They are not trade signals. Empirical outcomes must be measured on timestamped market data with transaction costs and leakage-safe validation.

references.author: Steve Nison
references.title: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques, 2nd edition
references.use: Candlestick construction, reversal and continuation concepts, contextual interpretation.

references.author: Thomas N. Bulkowski
references.title: Encyclopedia of Candlestick Charts
references.use: Pattern identification guidelines and statistical-performance research methodology.

patterns.name: Doji
patterns.definition: Very small real body relative to the full high-low range; open and close are nearly equal.
patterns.hypothesis: After a directional move it can signal hesitation or balance; in a range it may be ordinary noise.
patterns.context: Prior trend, location near a meaningful level, next-candle direction and volume.
patterns.failure: Continuation without follow-through or a break against the reversal idea.
patterns.caveat: Small bodies are common in low-volatility or illiquid periods. A doji alone is not a reversal signal.

patterns.name: Long-legged doji
patterns.definition: Very small real body with unusually long upper and lower shadows.
patterns.hypothesis: Shows substantial intrabar movement in both directions but little net progress; may reflect conflict or volatility.
patterns.context: Prior trend, session volatility, close location and next-candle range break.
patterns.failure: A break in the direction opposite the proposed reversal.
patterns.caveat: Long shadows can be caused by news or thin liquidity.

patterns.name: Dragonfly doji
patterns.definition: Open, close and high are near one another with a long lower shadow.
patterns.hypothesis: After a decline it may show rejection of lower prices; elsewhere it may simply show intrabar recovery.
patterns.context: Downtrend, support, close near high and subsequent higher close.
patterns.failure: A move below the candle low weakens the bullish rejection interpretation.
patterns.caveat: The textbook label does not guarantee a bullish outcome.

patterns.name: Gravestone doji
patterns.definition: Open, close and low are near one another with a long upper shadow.
patterns.hypothesis: After an advance it may show rejection of higher prices; elsewhere it can be indecision.
patterns.context: Prior uptrend, resistance, close near low and subsequent lower close.
patterns.failure: A move above the candle high weakens the bearish rejection interpretation.
patterns.caveat: Context and confirmation are essential.

patterns.name: Hammer
patterns.definition: Small real body near the upper end of the range, long lower shadow and little upper shadow.
patterns.hypothesis: After a decline it can indicate rejection of lower prices and a possible bullish reversal attempt.
patterns.context: Prior decline, support, relative shadow/body proportions and next-candle close above the hammer.
patterns.failure: A decisive break below the hammer low invalidates the local bullish-rejection thesis.
patterns.caveat: The same shape in an uptrend is not automatically a hammer signal.

patterns.name: Hanging man
patterns.definition: Hammer-like shape: small body near the top with a long lower shadow.
patterns.hypothesis: After an advance it can warn that sellers reached lower prices; bearish meaning needs confirmation.
patterns.context: Prior advance, resistance, next-candle weakness and volume context.
patterns.failure: A strong move above the high weakens the bearish warning.
patterns.caveat: Geometry resembles a hammer; trend context changes the interpretation.

patterns.name: Inverted hammer
patterns.definition: Small body near the lower end with a long upper shadow and little lower shadow.
patterns.hypothesis: After a decline it can show an attempted upward probe; buyers need follow-through.
patterns.context: Prior decline, support and a later close above the pattern high.
patterns.failure: A break below the pattern low before confirmation weakens the setup.
patterns.caveat: The long upper shadow also shows rejection; confirmation matters.

patterns.name: Shooting star
patterns.definition: Small body near the lower end with a long upper shadow and little lower shadow.
patterns.hypothesis: After an advance it may indicate rejection of higher prices and a bearish reversal attempt.
patterns.context: Prior advance, resistance, next-candle lower close and volume.
patterns.failure: A decisive move above the shooting-star high weakens the bearish thesis.
patterns.caveat: The same geometry in a downtrend is not automatically a shooting star.

patterns.name: Bullish engulfing
patterns.definition: A bullish real body engulfs the prior bearish real body.
patterns.hypothesis: After a decline it suggests a shift in short-term control toward buyers.
patterns.context: Prior decline, support, body size relative to recent candles and follow-through.
patterns.failure: A break below the two-candle low weakens the bullish thesis.
patterns.caveat: Body-engulfing does not require engulfing the full high-low range.

patterns.name: Bearish engulfing
patterns.definition: A bearish real body engulfs the prior bullish real body.
patterns.hypothesis: After an advance it suggests a shift in short-term control toward sellers.
patterns.context: Prior advance, resistance and subsequent lower close.
patterns.failure: A break above the two-candle high weakens the bearish thesis.
patterns.caveat: Body-engulfing does not require engulfing full shadows.

patterns.name: Piercing line
patterns.definition: After a bearish candle, a bullish candle opens lower and closes well into the prior real body, conventionally beyond its midpoint.
patterns.hypothesis: After a decline it can show buyers recovering a substantial part of the prior loss.
patterns.context: Prior decline, support, recovery depth and next-candle follow-through.
patterns.failure: A break below the two-candle low weakens the reversal attempt.
patterns.caveat: Opening-gap requirements can be awkward for intraday markets.

patterns.name: Dark cloud cover
patterns.definition: After a bullish candle, a bearish candle opens higher and closes well into the prior real body, conventionally below its midpoint.
patterns.hypothesis: After an advance it can show sellers erasing a substantial part of the prior gain.
patterns.context: Prior advance, resistance, penetration depth and follow-through.
patterns.failure: A break above the two-candle high weakens the bearish attempt.
patterns.caveat: Opening-gap conventions vary and may be less useful intraday.

patterns.name: Bullish harami
patterns.definition: A small second real body sits within the prior large bearish real body.
patterns.hypothesis: After a decline it can indicate selling pressure is slowing, not necessarily that a reversal has begun.
patterns.context: Prior decline, support, smaller second body and later upside break.
patterns.failure: Continuation below the pattern low argues against the bullish interpretation.
patterns.caveat: Inside-body relationship is a pause signal; confirmation is needed.

patterns.name: Bearish harami
patterns.definition: A small second real body sits within the prior large bullish real body.
patterns.hypothesis: After an advance it can indicate buying pressure is slowing.
patterns.context: Prior advance, resistance, smaller second body and later downside break.
patterns.failure: Continuation above the pattern high argues against the bearish interpretation.
patterns.caveat: Can occur frequently in sideways markets.

patterns.name: Morning star
patterns.definition: Three-candle sequence: strong bearish candle, small-bodied pause candle, then strong bullish candle closing well into the first body.
patterns.hypothesis: After a decline it represents a possible transition from selling to balance to buying.
patterns.context: Prior decline, support, third-candle close depth and volume.
patterns.failure: A break below the three-candle low weakens the bullish thesis.
patterns.caveat: Gap rules are market-dependent; intraday variants need explicit definitions.

patterns.name: Evening star
patterns.definition: Three-candle sequence: strong bullish candle, small-bodied pause candle, then strong bearish candle closing well into the first body.
patterns.hypothesis: After an advance it represents a possible transition from buying to balance to selling.
patterns.context: Prior advance, resistance, third-candle close depth and volume.
patterns.failure: A break above the three-candle high weakens the bearish thesis.
patterns.caveat: Gap rules are market-dependent; intraday variants need explicit definitions.

patterns.name: Tweezer bottom
patterns.definition: Two or more candles test nearly the same low and fail to sustain below it.
patterns.hypothesis: After a decline it may show repeated rejection of a price area.
patterns.context: Prior decline, ATR/tick-size tolerance, support and upside confirmation.
patterns.failure: A clean close below the repeated-low zone invalidates the rejection idea.
patterns.caveat: Equal lows need a tolerance rule; exact equality is too strict.

patterns.name: Tweezer top
patterns.definition: Two or more candles test nearly the same high and fail to sustain above it.
patterns.hypothesis: After an advance it may show repeated rejection of a price area.
patterns.context: Prior advance, ATR/tick-size tolerance, resistance and downside confirmation.
patterns.failure: A clean close above the repeated-high zone invalidates the rejection idea.
patterns.caveat: Equal highs need a tolerance rule; exact equality is too strict.

patterns.name: Inside bar
patterns.definition: Current candle high is below the previous high and its low is above the previous low.
patterns.hypothesis: Shows range contraction; the next range break may resolve in either direction.
patterns.context: Parent-candle location, prevailing trend, volatility contraction and breakout close/volume.
patterns.failure: A false break back into the parent range warns against assuming continuation.
patterns.caveat: A volatility/compression structure, not inherently bullish or bearish.

patterns.name: Outside bar
patterns.definition: Current candle makes a higher high and lower low than the previous candle.
patterns.hypothesis: Shows range expansion and two-sided activity; close location helps describe who finished stronger.
patterns.context: Close location within range, trend, relative volume and follow-through.
patterns.failure: A close near the opposite end or immediate range re-entry undermines directional read.
patterns.caveat: Direction cannot be inferred from range expansion alone.

patterns.name: Rising three methods
patterns.definition: Strong bullish candle, several smaller candles contained within its range, then strong bullish continuation candle.
patterns.hypothesis: In an uptrend it can represent a pause followed by buyers regaining control.
patterns.context: Established uptrend, contained pullback and final close above first-candle high.
patterns.failure: A break below the consolidation/first-candle low weakens continuation.
patterns.caveat: Textbook variants differ in candle count and containment rules.

patterns.name: Falling three methods
patterns.definition: Strong bearish candle, several smaller candles contained within its range, then strong bearish continuation candle.
patterns.hypothesis: In a downtrend it can represent a pause followed by sellers regaining control.
patterns.context: Established downtrend, contained bounce and final close below first-candle low.
patterns.failure: A break above the consolidation/first-candle high weakens continuation.
patterns.caveat: Textbook variants differ in candle count and containment rules.

patterns.name: Marubozu
patterns.definition: Large real body with very small or absent shadows.
patterns.hypothesis: Shows one-sided control during the candle; continuation is possible but not assured.
patterns.context: Body/range ratio, relative volume, trend alignment and nearby levels.
patterns.failure: Rapid retracement through the body suggests the impulse did not persist.
patterns.caveat: Large candles can mark exhaustion, news shocks or late entries.

patterns.name: Spinning top
patterns.definition: Small real body with meaningful upper and lower shadows.
patterns.hypothesis: Shows indecision or two-sided trade; context determines whether it is a pause or transition.
patterns.context: Prior move, location, range versus ATR and following candle.
patterns.failure: Breakout in prior trend without hesitation may make pause interpretation irrelevant.
patterns.caveat: Common in choppy markets; avoid over-counting.

patterns.name: Three white soldiers
patterns.definition: Three consecutive strong bullish candles with progressively higher closes and limited upper shadows.
patterns.hypothesis: Can show persistent buying pressure, especially after a decline or base.
patterns.context: Prior trend, candle-size progression, volume and distance from resistance.
patterns.failure: Sharp retracement below sequence base undermines momentum interpretation.
patterns.caveat: After an extended advance it may be late-stage strength.

patterns.name: Three black crows
patterns.definition: Three consecutive strong bearish candles with progressively lower closes and limited lower shadows.
patterns.hypothesis: Can show persistent selling pressure, especially after an advance or topping area.
patterns.context: Prior trend, candle-size progression, volume and distance from support.
patterns.failure: Sharp recovery above sequence base undermines bearish interpretation.
patterns.caveat: After an extended decline it may be late-stage weakness.
